role: does the encoder/decoder comparison and the accuracy of the fine-tuned specialist hold at smaller model sizes?
claim: Every fine-tuned result so far uses the 150M Ettin pair. Ettin releases the same paired architecture at smaller sizes. This sweep fine-tunes the 17M, 32M and 68M encoder and decoder on Banking77, SST-2 and MASSIVE English with the recipes already frozen for the 150M pair, and adds a small dev-selected learning-rate check because a rate chosen for 150M may undertrain a smaller model. Written before any model in this file was trained or scored.
size_note: 17M was not in the plan agreed with the user (32M and 68M); it is added because it is the cheapest to train and the most relevant to the FPGA question, and it runs after the other two at each stage.

recipes.banking77 and sst2: program2.json (encoder) and program2_decoder.json (decoder) with only the model, revision and learning rate replaced; the Program 1 dev rows are excluded from training and used for temperature; test is the Program 1 500-item test split
recipes.massive_en: the ettin_encoder and ettin_decoder blocks of primary_protocol.json with only the model, revision and learning rate replaced; official train, dev and test
recipes.banking77 decoder: batch 4 and label chunk 4 at every size, as pinned for the 150M decoder

learning_rates.selection: for each model and dataset, the rate with the lowest dev negative log-likelihood after temperature scaling. Test is not used to choose. Both the matched-rate row and the dev-selected row are reported.
learning_rates.which_models: encoders at all four sizes get both extra rates. Decoders are slow, so they get one extra rate, 1e-4, at 17M, 32M and 68M, and at 150M on Banking77 and MASSIVE only if the chain reaches that stage.

reference_rows: the 150M rows at 2e-5 are the existing seed-20261007 log-loss results (artifacts/program2, artifacts/program2-decoder, artifacts/primary); they are not retrained. The existing 150M MASSIVE encoder has no saved dev scores under this file's layout, so its dev negative log-likelihood is read from its metrics file.
order: encoders: 32M, 68M, 17M at 2e-5; then every encoder size at 5e-5 and 1e-4
decoders at 1e-4: 32M, 68M, 17M, then 150M on Banking77 and MASSIVE
metrics: accuracy, multiclass Brier, log loss and ECE on test after dev temperature, as in Program 1
batch-1 GPU latency p50 and p95 over the test items, timed after 20 warm-up items
parameter count of the trained model
encoder minus decoder at each size, and each model against its 150M counterpart
limits: One seed. The 150M results varied by about half a point across three seeds on these sets, so differences smaller than about a point between sizes are not evidence. The Banking77 and SST-2 test splits have 500 items.
